title: Two-Pointer Peaks
description: Two pointers and sliding windows turn O(n²) brute force into a single pass.

challenges.prompt: The array is sorted. Find two numbers that sum to a target using O(1) extra space. Which pattern fits?
options: Two pointers moving in from both ends
challenges.explanation: If the sum is too small, move the left pointer right; if too big, move the right pointer left. Sorting is what makes each move safe.

challenges.prompt: Check whether a string is a palindrome with two pointers.
challenges.explanation: hi must start at len(s) − 1, the last valid index. Starting at len(s) would read past the end of the string.

challenges.prompt: In the sorted pair-sum solution, each step moves one of the two pointers inward. Time complexity?
challenges.explanation: The pointers start n apart and close the gap by one each step, so there are at most n steps.

challenges.prompt: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place and return the new length. Which technique?
options: A slow pointer that writes and a fast pointer that reads
challenges.explanation: The fast pointer scans every element; when it finds a new value, the slow pointer writes it at the next slot. O(n) time, O(1) space.

challenges.prompt: Find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
options: Sliding window plus a set of characters in the window
challenges.explanation: Grow the window to the right; when a repeat appears, shrink from the left until it is gone. Each character enters and leaves the window once: O(n).

challenges.prompt: Return the maximum sum of any k consecutive elements, without re-adding the whole window each time.
challenges.explanation: Slide the window by adding the element that enters and subtracting the one that leaves. Recomputing the sum each time would cost O(n·k).

challenges.prompt: What is the time complexity of the sliding-window max sum above?
challenges.explanation: The first window costs k, then each of the remaining n − k steps is O(1). Total O(n).

challenges.prompt: In a variable-size sliding window, when should you move the left edge?
options: Only at the end of the array
Whenever the window breaks the problem's constraint
Never; only the right edge moves
challenges.explanation: Expand right greedily, then shrink from the left just enough to make the window valid again. That keeps it O(n).
